# FallKard — the Sovereign Locker

> FallKard turns the software you use into something you own. You get a kard (a portable, signed card),
> you open it, and your own workspace appears — on your own machine, in a look you choose. No account, no
> monthly rent; if the vendor vanishes, your copy is still yours. Runs entirely in your browser.

## In plain terms
Pull a kard -> open it (your workspace appears) -> pick your look (skins) -> it's yours, on your machine.
It's an alternative to the parts of software that cost the most and add the least: the front-end rebuilt
per client/brand, "white-label" theming sold per tenant, per-seat hosted tools, monthly subscription stacks,
and per-customer hosting. Build once, own forever, personalise infinitely.

## Who it's for
Agencies / solo builders who rebuild the same tool for every client (build once, skin per client, no re-host),
and individuals who want their own tools that feel like theirs and outlive any vendor.

## Under the hood (for builders)
A kard is a signed identity (Ed25519) carrying a skin, a structure, capabilities and an uncrossable budget.
Two witness-gated kernels drive it (the page inlines them, so the live logic is the gated logic):
- kard.mjs: mint / sign (self-sovereign) / verify / the uncrossable budget wall. Witness clean.
- flow.mjs: open + a counted cheap measurement (render only what you look at, recycle the rest). Cheap is
  measured, not claimed. Witness clean.
No LLM judge anywhere. The budget wall is real; selling kards/skins waits behind counsel; full node-to-node
federation is the next layer.
